The visible dark cell has crossed diagonals and upper/lower x feet. An underlying comma cannot be isolated. The directly visible x is put first; the alternative comma remains qualified. H has no trace of the cancellation.

Repeated diagonal hand strokes obscure the typed group notation. Left curves, middle feet and the last k-like portions remain, but do not select securely among C alternatives. The whole cancelled locus is preserved with its uncertainty.
A separate horizontal line lies below the typed Z. The lowered ell has its own crossing stroke; there is no doubled Z upright establishing blackboard bold.

The full cancelled dernière, including grave, remains on the baseline. Handwritten cohomologie stands above it, begins slightly right of its left edge and extends beyond its right edge. The word was rotated for a separate upright reading; no attachment leader is present.

The typed a lower bowl, b ascender/right bowl, l tall serif/stem, e crossbar and m upright/arches remain beneath the wider hand strokes t/e/m. The final typed m is visible as a distinct cell before the untouched ent; the alternative able is dropped. Placement is reproduced by overlapping nodes.

changes.shows: The added word is typed, with visible acute on é, on a raised line above the end of considération and des poids des. Its hand leader rises from below the cancelled final cell, runs under the added word and curls upward at the right.

The handwritten ana is on top of typed du at the original line end; logues is raised above cancelled même principe on the next line. The normal source line-break hyphen is joined, while these two relative overlay levels are retained. H drops du. The apparent dot after logues belongs to the typed i beneath it, so no new stop is added.
A separate typed final e remains at the right of oral with a diagonal cancellation through it. It is not an accent or a live terminal e.

Handwritten développé is above également, beginning slightly before it. Both acute accents are visible. A leader starts after était below the baseline, curves upward beneath the addition and curls at its right end.

Between p and e there is a tall left-serifed stem with a broad foot, plus a rounded impression extending left of the stem and two partly fused right curves. The neighboring plain l supplies a direct shape control. A qualified o/l or b/l overprint represents the extra ink; neither a clean b nor a clean l alone accounts for it.

Cancelled limitée is fully readable on the baseline. The hand addition starts above and slightly before it; a leader begins after the old word, curves upward under the addition, and turns up at the right. The placement and leader are reproduced.

Each opening and closing pair consists of two high downward typewriter strokes. No left- or right-pointing angle shapes occur at these four loci.
